sentences.text:
Appearance:
 Shri Nilesh Agrawal - Advocate for the petitioner.
 Shri Hemant Sharma - G.A. for State.

2] This petition has been filed by the petitioner under Section 528 of B.N.S.S./482 of Cr.P.C. for quashment of FIR lodged against the petitioner at Crime No.338 of 2010 registered at Police Station Mhow, District - Indore under Sections 498A, 294, 323, 506(2), 406 of IPC read with Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.

3] Counsel for the petitioner, at the outset, has drawn the attention of this Court to the compromise application filed in the trial Court, whereby the complainant/wife had also agreed to compromise the matter, and although the aforesaid application was allowed, however, it was allowed in part only,
as so far as the offence under Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act is concerned, the Court held that it is not a compoundable offence.

Counsel has also submitted that the case itself is pending since 2010,
and now that the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:29413 2 MCRC-43259-2025 parties have entered into a compromise, the inherent powers of this Court may be invoked to quash the FIR so far as it relates to Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act only, as the other offences have already been compromised between the parties.
4] Counsel for the State has submitted that appropriate order may be passed.

Manish Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109819987/
1 5] On due consideration, this Court finds that since the matter relates to a matrimonial dispute,
which has already been compromised, and only on technical issue that Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act is not compoundable, the case is still kept pending in the trial Court, this Court finds that no purpose would be served to keep the trial pending when the parties have already settled the matter out of the Court, which also relates to a matrimonial dispute only.

sentences.text: In view of same, this Court has no hesitation to quash the FIR in its entirety, including Section 4 of the of Dowry Prohibition Act.
6] Accordingly, the petition stands allowed and the FIR lodged at Crime No.338 of 2010, which now relates to section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act only is hereby quashed.
Pursuant to which, the criminal case pending in the trial Court is also hereby quashed.
7] With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed and disposed of.

(SUBODH ABHYANKAR) JUDGE Pankaj Manish Mishra vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/109819987/
